statute_title: Driving Under the Influence of Liquor or Controlled Substances
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle
On any highway, road, street, or public or private parking area
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor, toluene, or any controlled substance
Or had a BAC of .08 or higher
mandatory_minimum: 10-60 hours community service (first); 10 days to 6 months (second); 1-3 years (third+)
enhancements: Child under 13 in vehicle (additional 6 months mandatory)
notes: Rhode Island has a tiered BAC system for first offenses: .08-.10, .10-.15, and .15+. Implied consent under § 31-27-2.1. Chemical test refusal triggers admin suspension. Community service required for first offense. Victim impact panel required.

elements: Defendant operated a vehicle while under the influence
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
No prior DUI convictions within 5 years
mandatory_minimum: 10-60 hours community service; DUI school; 30-180 day license suspension
enhancements: BAC .15+ (mandatory 10-60 hours community service or up to 10 days jail)
notes: Tiered first-offense penalties based on BAC level. BAC .08-.10: minimum 10 hours community service. BAC .10-.15: minimum 10 days community service or up to 6 months jail. BAC .15+: enhanced penalties. Hardship license available.

elements: Defendant operated a vehicle while under the influence
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
One or more prior DUI convictions within 5 years
notes: Second offense: 1-2 year license suspension, mandatory IID. Third offense:  felony, 2-3 year suspension, vehicle seizure possible. Look-back period is 5 years.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle
While under the influence of any controlled substance as defined in Chapter 21-28
Or under the influence of toluene or any intoxicating substance
To a degree rendering the defendant incapable of safely driving
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: No per se drug limit. Prosecution must prove impairment. Includes prescription medications. Drug Recognition Expert (DRE) evaluation used for evidence.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
In a manner so as to indicate either a willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common plea-down from DUI. Adds points to driving record. May result in license suspension.

statute_title: Duty to Stop in Event of Accident — Injury or Death
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop at the scene
Defendant failed to give name, address, and registration and render aid
notes: Leaving scene resulting in death or serious injury is a felony. Property damage only is a misdemeanor. Must report to nearest police within 24 hours.

elements: Defendant operated a vehicle while under the influence
Defendant's impaired driving caused the death of another person
mandatory_minimum: 5 years (no suspended sentence or probation for first 5 years)
notes: Rhode Island has a specific DUI-death statute. Minimum 5 years mandatory, no suspension or probation. License revocation for 2 years. May also be charged as voluntary or involuntary manslaughter.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
By negligent or reckless operation of a motor vehicle
notes: Rhode Island does not have a separate vehicular manslaughter statute. Vehicular deaths may be charged as manslaughter (§ 11-23-2) or under the DUI-death statute (§ 31-27-2.2) depending on circumstances.

statute_title: Driving While License Suspended or Revoked
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a public highway
Defendant's license was suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
notes: Additional suspension imposed upon conviction. DUI-related suspension violations carry mandatory jail time. May result in vehicle impoundment.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (basic); Felony (if endangerment or high speed)
elements: A police officer in uniform gave a visual or audible signal to stop
Defendant willfully failed to stop or attempted to elude the officer
The officer was operating a marked vehicle
notes: Eluding that results in injury or death or involves high-speed pursuit elevates to a felony. License suspension mandatory.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (personal use under 2014 reform); Felony (larger amounts)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed
A controlled substance
Without a valid prescription or legal authorization
notes: Rhode Island reclassified simple possession as a misdemeanor in 2014 (previously felony). Personal-use amounts only. Distribution quantities remain felony.

offense_class: Civil violation (1 oz or less); Misdemeanor (over 1 oz)
penalty_max: $150 fine (1 oz or less); 1 year (over 1 oz)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed marijuana
In any amount
notes: Rhode Island legalized recreational marijuana in 2022 (RI Cannabis Act). Adults 21+ may possess up to 1 oz. Over 1 oz without license is an offense. Medical marijuana legal since 2006.

elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed
Cocaine (Schedule II)
Without a valid prescription
notes: Simple possession reclassified as misdemeanor in 2014. Distribution-quantity possession remains a felony. Cocaine is Schedule II in Rhode Island.

elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed
Methamphetamine (Schedule II)
Without a valid prescription
notes: Simple possession reclassified to misdemeanor in 2014. Manufacturing meth is a serious felony. Methamphetamine less prevalent in RI than in many states.

penalty_min: 10 years (1+ kg cocaine); 25 years (5+ kg cocaine)
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver
A controlled substance in a trafficking quantity
mandatory_minimum: 10 years (1+ kg cocaine); 25 years (5+ kg cocaine); varies by substance
notes: Trafficking thresholds and mandatory minimums vary by substance. No parole or suspended sentence for certain quantities. Asset forfeiture provisions apply.

statute_title: Manufacture, Delivery, or Possession with Intent to Deliver
penalty_max: 30 years (Schedule I-II); 20 years (Schedule III-IV); 5 years (Schedule V)
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver
A controlled substance
To another person
notes: Delivery near school (within 300 yards) carries enhanced mandatory minimum under § 21-28-4.07. Second offense doubles maximum penalty.

elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured or attempted to manufacture
A controlled substance
enhancements: Manufacturing in presence of a minor
notes: Manufacturing carries the same penalties as distribution. Methamphetamine manufacturing carries especially severe consequences.

elements: Defendant knowingly used or possessed with intent to use
Drug paraphernalia
For the purpose of using a controlled substance
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor (felony)
notes: Delivery of paraphernalia is a separate, more serious offense. Delivery to a minor under 18 carries enhanced penalties. Harm reduction equipment (clean syringes) exempt under harm reduction laws.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
With the intent to deliver to another person
Intent may be inferred from quantity, packaging, or other evidence
notes: Intent inferred from circumstantial evidence. Same penalties as delivery. Near-school enhancement applies.

elements: Defendant unlawfully killed another human being
With malice aforethought
With premeditation and deliberation
Or during the commission of certain felonies (felony murder)
notes: Rhode Island does not have the death penalty (abolished 1984). First degree murder carries mandatory life without parole. Includes felony murder during commission of specified felonies.

elements: Defendant unlawfully killed another human being
With malice aforethought
Without premeditation or deliberation
notes: Second degree murder is intentional killing without premeditation, or killing with depraved indifference to human life. Eligible for parole after serving the mandatory minimum.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
In the heat of passion upon adequate provocation
Without premeditation or malice aforethought
notes: Rhode Island's manslaughter statute encompasses both voluntary (heat of passion) and involuntary (negligence) manslaughter. Up to 30 years imprisonment.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Through criminal negligence or recklessness
Without intent to kill
notes: Involuntary manslaughter is prosecuted under the general manslaughter statute. Includes negligent vehicular deaths. Sentence depends on circumstances and culpability.

elements: Defendant committed assault or assault and battery
With a dangerous weapon
Or resulting in serious bodily injury
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer (§ 11-5-5)
notes: Felony assault covers assaults with dangerous weapons, those causing serious injury, and assaults on protected persons. Assault with intent to commit murder (§ 11-5-1) is punishable up to 20 years.

elements: Defendant committed an assault or assault and battery
Upon another person
notes: Simple assault and battery is a misdemeanor. Rhode Island defines assault as an unlawful attempt or offer to do violence and battery as an unlawful touching.

elements: Defendant committed an unlawful touching or physical harm upon another person
notes: Rhode Island combines assault and battery under the same statute. Battery is the actual physical contact component.

elements: Defendant took money or personal property from the person or presence of another
By force, violence, or intimidation
Against the will of the victim
notes: Robbery is a felony punishable by up to life imprisonment in Rhode Island. No separate degrees — all robbery under one statute.

elements: Defendant committed robbery
While armed with a dangerous weapon
Or displayed what appeared to be a dangerous weapon
notes: Rhode Island does not have a separate armed robbery statute — all robbery is under § 11-39-1 with up to life imprisonment. Armed component is an aggravating factor at sentencing.

elements: Defendant seized, confined, or carried away another person
By force, threat, or deception
Without lawful authority or consent
notes: Kidnapping with ransom demand carries 20-year mandatory minimum. Child kidnapping may trigger additional charges. Second-degree kidnapping (§ 11-26-1.1) has a 10-year minimum.

penalty_max: 20 years (first degree); 10 years (second degree); 5 years (third degree)
elements: Defendant knowingly set fire to or caused an explosion in
An occupied dwelling or building
Resulting in damage
notes: First degree (§ 11-4-2): occupied dwelling. Second degree (§ 11-4-3): unoccupied building. Third degree (§ 11-4-4): other property. Arson causing death may be charged as murder.

elements: Defendant intended to cause the death of another person
Defendant took a substantial step toward the commission of murder
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Attempted murder prosecuted under the general attempt statute and assault with intent to commit murder (§ 11-5-1). Punishable by up to 20 years.

statute_title: Felony Assault with a Dangerous Weapon
elements: Defendant committed assault or assault and battery
With a dangerous weapon
notes: Dangerous weapon includes firearms, knives, and any instrument capable of causing serious bodily injury. Assault with intent to commit murder (§ 11-5-1) carries up to 20 years.

elements: Defendant took personal property of another
Without the owner's consent
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Rhode Island's felony larceny threshold is $1,500. Larceny from a building (§ 11-41-4) is separate. Receiving stolen goods (§ 11-41-2) has similar thresholds.

elements: Defendant took personal property of another
Value exceeded $1,500
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Rhode Island uses $1,500 as the felony threshold. No 'grand theft' terminology — it is simply 'larceny' with the value determining the offense level.

elements: Defendant took personal property of another
Value was under $1,500
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Misdemeanor larceny for property under $1,500. Third larceny conviction becomes a felony regardless of value.

elements: Defendant willfully concealed merchandise offered for sale
While on the merchant's premises
With intent to convert the merchandise without paying
notes: Willful concealment creates a presumption of intent to convert. Civil demand provisions allow merchants to seek damages. Value thresholds follow larceny statute.

elements: Defendant broke and entered a dwelling house or building of another
With intent to commit a crime therein
notes: Breaking and entering a dwelling at nighttime carries up to life imprisonment. Non-dwelling or daytime burglary carries up to 10 years under § 11-8-2.

statute_title: Burglary of a Dwelling at Night
elements: Defendant broke and entered a dwelling house of another
During nighttime
With intent to commit a crime therein
notes: Nighttime dwelling burglary is the most serious burglary charge — up to life imprisonment. Daytime dwelling burglary or other structure burglary under § 11-8-2.

statute_title: Unauthorized Use of a Motor Vehicle
elements: Defendant took, drove, or used a motor vehicle belonging to another
Without the owner's consent
notes: Rhode Island has a specific motor vehicle theft statute. May also be charged as larceny if permanent deprivation intended.

elements: Defendant received, bought, or concealed stolen property
Knowing or having reason to believe the property was stolen
notes: Same felony threshold as larceny ($1,500). Knowledge of stolen status may be inferred from circumstances.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously destroyed or injured property of another
notes: Felony threshold for malicious damage is $1,000. Graffiti has a separate statute. Restitution commonly ordered.

elements: Defendant entered or remained upon property of another
After being forbidden to do so by the owner or authorized person
Or entered property that was fenced, posted, or otherwise secured
enhancements: Trespass with intent to commit a crime (burglary)
notes: Notice may be given by posting signs, fencing, or personal communication. Trespass with criminal intent may be charged as burglary.

statute_title: Malicious Damage to or Destruction of Property
elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously injured or destroyed tangible property of another
notes: Rhode Island uses 'malicious damage' rather than 'criminal mischief.' Same statute as vandalism. Offense level depends on damage value.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first offense simple assault); Felony (aggravated or repeat)
elements: Defendant committed an assault or assault and battery
Against a family or household member (spouse, former spouse, cohabitant, co-parent, or dating partner)
notes: Rhode Island Domestic Violence Prevention Act (§ 12-29) applies DV designation to underlying criminal charges. Domestic strangulation is a specific felony. Firearms prohibition upon conviction.

elements: Defendant committed assault and battery upon a family or household member
notes: Charged as simple assault and battery with domestic violence classification. Batterer's intervention program mandatory. No-contact order typically issued.

statute_title: Cruelty to or Neglect of a Child
elements: Defendant was a person responsible for the care of a child
Defendant knowingly or negligently exposed the child to conditions that endangered health, welfare, or safety
notes: Rhode Island broadly defines child endangerment. Includes exposure to drug use, leaving children unattended, and failure to provide medical care. Mandatory reporters under § 40-11-3.

elements: Defendant caused nonaccidental physical injury to a child
Defendant was a parent, guardian, or caretaker
notes: Serious physical abuse may carry enhanced penalties. Mandatory reporting by certain professionals. DCYF involvement in all cases.

elements: A valid protective order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully violated a term of the order
enhancements: Second or subsequent violation within 3 years (felony)
notes: Mandatory minimum 24 hours for first violation. Second violation within 3 years is a felony. No-contact order violations treated the same.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Felony (subsequent or with threat of death)
elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously engaged in a course of conduct
Directed at a specific person
That seriously alarmed, annoyed, or bothered the person
That would cause a reasonable person to suffer substantial emotional distress
enhancements: Violation of protective order during stalking
notes: Course of conduct means two or more acts. Cyberstalking specifically addressed under § 11-52-4.2. Protective orders available.

elements: Defendant, with intent to harass, annoy, or alarm another person
Made unwanted communications or contact
After being asked to stop
notes: Includes telephone harassment, electronic harassment, and repeated unwanted contact. May escalate to stalking charges if course of conduct is established.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation of an Elderly Person
elements: Defendant willfully abused, neglected, or exploited an elderly person (age 60+)
Or a person who was severely impaired
notes: Rhode Island has a specific elder abuse statute. Financial exploitation of the elderly is separately addressed. Mandatory reporting under § 42-66-8.

statute_title: Carrying a Pistol Without a License
elements: Defendant carried a pistol or revolver
On or about their person or in a vehicle
Without a valid license to carry
mandatory_minimum: 1 year (no suspension or probation for first year)
notes: Rhode Island requires a license to carry a concealed handgun. Supreme Court's Bruen decision (2022) affected licensing. Long guns do not require a license. No constitutional carry.

statute_title: Possession of a Firearm by Prohibited Person
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant was a person prohibited from possessing firearms (convicted felon, fugitive, etc.)
notes: Mandatory minimum 2 years, no suspended sentence. Includes persons convicted of crimes of violence, drug offenses, and fugitives from justice. Federal 18 U.S.C. § 922(g) also applies.

statute_title: Carrying a Concealed Weapon Without a License
elements: Defendant carried a concealed pistol, revolver, or other weapon
Without a valid license to carry
notes: Rhode Island concealed carry licenses issued by AG or local police chief. Post-Bruen, licensing cannot be based solely on 'proper cause' — must be shall-issue if objective criteria met.

statute_title: Discharging a Firearm in a Compact Area
elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
In a thickly settled or compact area
Or in a manner that endangered the safety of others
notes: Discharge resulting in injury may be charged as assault with a dangerous weapon. Municipal ordinances may impose additional restrictions.

elements: Defendant knowingly and without authorization used personal identifying information of another
To obtain money, credit, goods, services, or anything of value
notes: Rhode Island Identity Theft Protection Act. Restitution ordered. Includes use of SSN, financial account numbers, and biometric data. AG maintains identity theft database.

elements: Defendant was entrusted with money or property
By virtue of employment, office, or trust
Defendant fraudulently converted the money or property to personal use
notes: Rhode Island has a specific embezzlement statute. Same felony threshold as larceny ($1,500). Public officer embezzlement separately addressed.

elements: Defendant, with intent to defraud
Falsely made, forged, altered, or counterfeited a written instrument
Or knowingly uttered a forged instrument
notes: Covers checks, deeds, contracts, and official documents. Uttering (passing) a forged instrument is the same offense.

elements: Defendant made or possessed counterfeited currency, coin, or valuable instrument
With intent to defraud
notes: Currency counterfeiting typically prosecuted federally. State charges apply to counterfeit documents, checks, and instruments.

elements: Defendant issued a check or draft
Knowing at the time of issuance there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: Defendant must be given notice and 10 days to make the check good. Payment within that period is a defense.

elements: Defendant knowingly presented or caused to be presented
A false or fraudulent claim or statement to an insurance company
For the purpose of obtaining payment or benefit
notes: Rhode Island Insurance Fraud Prevention Act. Includes auto, health, property, and workers' compensation fraud. Restitution and civil penalties may also apply.

elements: Defendant used a credit card or credit card number
Without authorization of the cardholder
To obtain property, services, or money
notes: Rhode Island has specific credit card crime statutes covering theft, fraudulent use, and trafficking in stolen card numbers.

elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Involving proceeds of specified unlawful activity
With knowledge that the property represents proceeds of unlawful activity
notes: Rhode Island Money Laundering Act. Fine may be up to $500,000 or twice the amount laundered. Asset forfeiture provisions apply.

statute_title: Obtaining Money or Goods Under False Pretenses
elements: Defendant obtained money, goods, or other property from another
By false pretenses, representation, or fraud
With intent to cheat and defraud
notes: General fraud statute. Same felony threshold as larceny. Specific fraud statutes may apply for insurance, securities, or computer fraud.

elements: Defendant engaged in sexual penetration with another person
By force or coercion
Or the victim was mentally incapacitated or physically helpless
Or the victim was under 13
mandatory_minimum: 10 years (no parole for first 10 years); 25 years (if victim under 13)
notes: First degree sexual assault carries severe mandatory minimums. Victim under 13 triggers 25-year mandatory minimum. Lifetime sex offender registration. GPS monitoring.

elements: Defendant engaged in sexual contact with another person
By force or coercion
Or the victim was unable to consent
notes: Rhode Island uses 'sexual assault' rather than 'rape.' Second degree involves sexual contact (not penetration). First degree (§ 11-37-2) involves penetration. Sex offender registration required.

elements: Defendant intentionally exposed private parts
In a public place or where likely to be observed
Under circumstances that caused affront or alarm
notes: First offense is a misdemeanor. Subsequent conviction is a felony. May require sex offender registration depending on circumstances.

elements: Defendant offered or agreed to pay money or other consideration
For the purpose of engaging in sexual conduct
notes: Rhode Island criminalized indoor prostitution in 2009 (previously legal). Buying sex is criminal. Trafficking and promoting prostitution carry severe penalties.

elements: Defendant knowingly produced, possessed, or distributed
Visual material depicting a child under 18 engaged in sexual conduct
notes: Federal charges commonly apply. Rhode Island has specific child exploitation statutes. Sex offender registration required. Internet luring separately addressed.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register, verify, or update information
Within the time period required
notes: Rhode Island sex offender registration under Chapter 11-37.1. Registration period varies by risk level. Verification required annually or quarterly depending on classification.

offense_class: Felony (under 14); Misdemeanor (14-16 depending on age gap)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual penetration with a minor
Below the age of consent
Defendant was older than the age specified by statute
notes: Age of consent is 16 in Rhode Island. Third degree sexual assault (§ 11-37-6) covers various non-force situations including statutory. Under 14 triggers first degree charges.

elements: Defendant engaged in fighting or threatening behavior
Or made unreasonable noise
Or used abusive or obscene language in a public place
With intent to cause inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm
notes: Commonly charged alongside other offenses. Broad statute covering public disturbances, fighting, and offensive conduct.

elements: Defendant knowingly and willfully resisted a peace officer
In making an arrest
By using or threatening to use physical force
notes: Rhode Island prohibits resisting even an unlawful arrest. Remedy is through legal channels, not physical resistance. Force against officer may result in felony assault charges.

elements: Defendant willfully obstructed, resisted, or opposed
A public officer or person assisting a public officer
In serving or executing legal process or in performing a lawful duty
notes: Includes providing false information, hiding evidence, and physically obstructing officers. More serious obstruction may be charged as accessory after the fact.

offense_class: Varies — up to 6 months for criminal contempt
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a lawful order of the court
Or engaged in disorderly behavior in the presence of the court
notes: Both civil (remedial) and criminal (punitive) contempt. Court has broad discretion. Due process protections apply.

elements: Person appeared intoxicated in a public place
Person was incapacitated or posed a danger to self or others
notes: Rhode Island generally treats public intoxication as a public health matter. Intoxicated persons may be taken to a treatment facility. Not typically prosecuted as a standalone criminal offense.

elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal recognizance
Defendant was required to appear in court
Defendant willfully failed to appear as required
notes: Bail forfeiture and bench warrant issued. Failure to appear in felony case is itself a felony. Charged in addition to the original offense.

elements: Defendant knowingly provided false information to law enforcement
Regarding the commission of a crime
notes: Includes filing false police reports and making false 911 calls. False bomb threats charged under separate, more serious statutes.

elements: Defendant threatened to commit a crime of violence
Against another person or their property
With intent to place the person in fear of injury or damage
enhancements: Threat against school or public building
notes: Rhode Island criminalizes threats of violence and extortion. Bomb threats and threats against schools carry enhanced penalties under separate statutes.

elements: Defendant, being under oath or affirmation
Willfully and falsely testified to a material matter
In a judicial proceeding or before a body authorized to take testimony
notes: Perjury requires materiality and willfulness. Corroboration typically required. False statements outside judicial proceedings may be charged under other statutes.

elements: Defendant offered, gave, or promised money or value
To a public official
With intent to influence the official's conduct in an official capacity
enhancements: Bribery of a judge or juror
notes: Both the giver and receiver may be charged. Public official forfeits office upon conviction. Separate statutes for bribery of jurors and witnesses.

elements: Defendant was in lawful custody
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape from custody
notes: Sentence for escape runs consecutive to original sentence. Aiding escape is a separate offense. Includes escape from prison, jail, and lawful custody during transport.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first non-aggravated); Felony (aggravated, malicious, or subsequent)
elements: Defendant unnecessarily or cruelly beat or tortured an animal
Or failed to provide necessary sustenance, shelter, or medical care
notes: Rhode Island has both misdemeanor and felony animal cruelty statutes. Malicious torture is a felony. Animal fighting is separately prohibited. Court may order forfeiture of animals.

offense_class: Varies — court may revoke and impose original sentence
penalty_max: Original sentence for the underlying offense
fine_max: Original fine for the underlying offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation with specific conditions
Defendant violated one or more conditions of probation
notes: Court may continue, modify, or revoke probation. Hearing required. Technical violations may be treated differently than new criminal conduct. Burden of proof is preponderance.

offense_class: Varies — Parole Board may revoke parole
elements: Defendant was released on parole with specific conditions
Defendant violated one or more conditions of parole
notes: Rhode Island Parole Board determines revocation. Hearing required. May serve remainder of sentence. Technical violations distinguished from new criminal conduct.

elements: Defendant aided, assisted, abetted, counseled, or advised another
In the commission of a criminal offense
With intent to promote or facilitate the crime
notes: Rhode Island treats accessories as principals. Mere presence at the scene is insufficient. Must have intent and affirmative action.

offense_class: Same as or one grade below the target offense
elements: Defendant intended to commit a specific crime
Defendant took a substantial step toward the commission of the crime
Beyond mere preparation
notes: Attempt penalties generally proportional to the completed offense. Abandonment may be a defense if voluntary and complete.

offense_class: Same as or one grade below the target offense (max 20 years for most serious)
penalty_max: 20 years (conspiracy to commit felony); 1 year (conspiracy to commit misdemeanor)
elements: Two or more persons agreed to commit a criminal offense
At least one overt act was committed in furtherance of the conspiracy
notes: Conspiracy to commit a felony is itself a felony. Requires an overt act. Withdrawal is a defense if communicated to co-conspirators and steps taken to prevent the crime.
